source.title: A Trend Factor for the Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
source.publication: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 60(7), 2025, 3116-3153

hypothesis: A causal rolling elastic-net aggregation of the paper's most important technical trend indicators predicts the next-week cross-section of liquid Binance perpetual returns and produces a robust net long-short factor.
feature_policy: Source-driven exception to the usual compact-feature rule: use exactly the eight highest-ranked CTREND variables reported in the paper supplement, translated to available ml4t-engineer features: Bollinger middle distance, CCI20, MACD12-26 normalized by price, MACD-minus-9d-signal normalized by price, 5d SMA distance, Bollinger upper distance, 3d SMA distance, and stochastic %K14.
universe: Each Monday, eligible Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals with at least 90 exact complete UTC days and all features valid; keep top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.
feature_mapping: Within each Monday cross-section, map every raw feature to percentile rank centered at zero. No full-sample scaling.
model: One rolling ElasticNetCV model per rebalance. Train on the preceding 52 completed feature weeks, embargo the immediately preceding week, preserve entire weeks in four chronological CV folds, l1_ratio=[0.1,0.5,0.9], alpha grid=1e-5..1e-2 (7 log-spaced values). Hyperparameters are selected strictly inside each training window and are not external strategy trials.
portfolio: Market-neutral weekly long top predicted-return quintile / short bottom quintile, 0.5 gross each side.
execution: All technical features use data through Sunday close. Rebalance at Monday 00:00 UTC open. The one-week training embargo prevents using the current execution price to finalize the latest training label.
development_gate: Rolling model mean weekly rank IC >=0.02, HAC p<0.05, positive winner-minus-loser return, and net development Sharpe >0.70.
success_gate: OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS mean rank IC >=0.02 with HAC p<0.05; positive at 2x costs; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest asset positive; DSR reported and must be >=0.95 when computed.
deviations_from_paper: Uses eight highest-importance variables rather than all 28 to keep the adaptation auditable and computationally bounded.
Uses lagged quote volume for liquidity eligibility instead of historical market capitalization.
Uses equal-weight long-short portfolio rather than value weighting because point-in-time market cap is unavailable.
Binance perpetual funding is unavailable in the OHLCV panel and is not modeled.
